meta.title: Terms of Service
meta.description: The terms for using WattPrint, a household electricity tracker and bill forecast.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms (“Terms”) apply when you use WattPrint: the landing page and the dashboard. By creating an account or continuing to use the service, you agree to these Terms.

service.title: 1. What WattPrint is
service.body: WattPrint shows your home's electricity use, estimates how much each appliance uses, forecasts your electricity bill and suggests ways to save. Every figure is for information: per-appliance numbers are estimates made from the main meter, not separate measurements, and a forecast bill can differ from your utility's bill. The real bill is always the one your electricity company sends.

accounts.title: 2. Accounts and security
accounts.body: When you create an account, you agree to:

items.confidential: Keep your sign-in details to yourself.
items.notify: Tell us soon if you suspect someone else got into your account.
items.responsible: Be responsible for everything done under your account.

acceptableUse.title: 3. Using it properly
acceptableUse.body: You agree not to misuse the service or help others to. In particular, you will not:

items.laws: Break Vietnamese law, including the rules on cybersecurity and personal data protection.
items.security: Try to get past sign-in, rate limits or other safeguards without clear permission.
items.abuse: Run denial-of-service attacks, guess passwords automatically or reach other people's data.

home.title: 4. Your home and its members
home.body: Each account belongs to one home. The owner is the person who set the home up; members use the home's data together, and a viewer can only read. The sample homes on the sign-in page are public recordings from research datasets (REFIT, Plegma, ENERTALK) replayed for you to try, not homes of WattPrint users. Trial guest accounts are deleted after 24 hours, when the next trial guest arrives.

assistant.title: 5. The Wappi assistant
assistant.body: Wappi is an automated system, not a person. Figures in its answers come from your home's data, but its explanations can be wrong or incomplete, so do not treat them as professional advice. Do not type sensitive details into the chat: phone numbers, ID numbers, emails, card and account numbers are replaced by a label before they are stored, but this only spots familiar number formats, not names or addresses.

liability.title: 6. Limit of liability
liability.body: The service is provided “as is”, with no warranty of any kind, express or implied, as far as the law allows. We are not liable for indirect or consequential loss from using or not being able to use the service, including decisions about electricity or money made from estimated or forecast figures.

termination.title: 7. Ending and deleting your account
termination.body: You can end these Terms at any time by deleting your account from the account menu in the dashboard (see the Privacy Policy for what is erased). We may suspend or end accounts that break these Terms.

law.title: 8. Governing law and contact
law.body: These Terms are governed by Vietnamese law. For any question, contact ntgiang141105@gmail.com.

meta.title: Privacy Policy
meta.description: How WattPrint collects, uses, shares and deletes your data.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page says what data WattPrint collects, who receives it, how long it is kept and how you delete it. It is written with Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 91/2025/QH15) and Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP in mind.

controller.title: 1. Who is responsible for your data
controller.body: Your data is managed, and answered for, by an individual:
controller.name: Nguyễn Trường Giang

collected.title: 2. Data we collect
collected.body: Only what the service needs to run:

items.account: Account: email and name (typed at sign-up, or taken from your Google account if you sign in with Google). Keycloak keeps the password as a hash; we cannot read it.
items.session: Sign-in session: an access token in a cookie, and the IP address that the server and Keycloak log to stop abuse.
items.home: Your home: its name, province or city, number of people, floor area, home type, billing cycle day and the notification choices you set.
items.energy: Electricity: your home's meter readings, per-appliance estimates computed from them, forecast bills, alerts and savings plans.
items.assistant: Chats with Wappi: questions and answers are stored with your account. Phone numbers, ID numbers, emails, card and account numbers are replaced by a label before they are stored or sent on.
items.voice: Voice: when you speak to Wappi, the audio is turned into text; when you listen to an answer, the spoken audio is kept so it need not be made again.
items.guest: Trial guests: a temporary account with no real email, deleted after 24 hours (expired ones are cleared when a new guest arrives).

sharing.title: 3. Who receives your data
sharing.body: Some parts of the service are handled by others. We send only what each needs, and some of them are outside Vietnam:

items.ai: OpenRouter and AstralX (Wappi's language models): your question with personal details masked, and the figures Wappi's tools look up from your home's data to answer it.
items.voice: AstralX (voice): the audio you record to turn into text, and the answer to be read aloud.
items.weather: OpenWeather (weather): only the province or city coordinates of your home, never your address or name.
items.google: Google (sign-in, if you choose it): Google knows that you sign in to WattPrint its way.

sharing.abroad: Each of them has its own policy on the data it gets; read it if that matters to you. We do not use your data for advertising and we have built no advertising trackers into the service.

bases.title: 4. Why we may handle your data
bases.body: Each use rests on a clear ground:

contract.title: To provide the service
contract.body: Creating your account, signing you in, showing electricity and bills, running Wappi.

consent.title: You agree
consent.body: You sign up yourself, turn email notifications on yourself and choose to talk to Wappi. Silence or a pre-ticked box is not agreement.

interests.title: Protecting the service
interests.body: Rate limits, blocking attacks and spotting unusual access.

statutory.title: What the law requires
statutory.body: Giving information when a competent authority makes a valid request.

cookies.title: 5. Cookies and browser storage
cookies.body: We use no advertising or behaviour-tracking cookies. Only what the service needs to run:

items.session: Three sign-in cookies (.access, .refresh, .id), set HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, plus Secure in production. While you sign in there is also a short-lived cookie (10 minutes) that confirms the sign-in, and Keycloak sets its own session cookies on its own domain.
items.theme: Your light, dark or system choice is kept in your own browser.

retention.title: 6. How long we keep it
retention.body: Data is kept while the account exists, except for:

items.readings: Per-minute readings and per-appliance estimates: the last 400 days; older ones are deleted automatically.
items.rollups: Hourly and daily totals: kept until you delete your account.
items.account: Profile, chats, alerts and plans: kept until you delete your account.
items.guest: Trial guest accounts: 24 hours, cleared when a new guest arrives.

rights.title: 7. Your rights
rights.body: Under Law No. 91/2025/QH15 and Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP you have these rights over your data. Send a request to the email in section 1; we answer within the time the law sets.

items.access: To know and see your data.
items.correct: To correct wrong data. You can edit your home and notification choices in settings; for your name or email, write to the email in section 1.
items.withdraw: To withdraw consent, for example by turning email notifications off in settings.
items.erase: To ask for your data to be deleted: do it yourself right away from the account menu, see section 8.
items.complain: To complain, report or sue if you think your data was handled unlawfully.

deletion.title: 8. Deleting your account
deletion.body: Open the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar and choose Delete account. Your profile, chats, savings plans, the alerts you set, your choices and your sign-in account are deleted at once (if deleting the sign-in account fails, you are asked to try again). If you are the only person in your home, the home goes too, with its alerts, all its meter readings and its totals. The data is deleted from the running system.
deletion.limit: If other people are still in your home we cannot delete it yet, because their data is not yours to delete: ask them to leave first. If you cannot use the menu, send the request to the email in section 1.

ai.title: 9. The Wappi assistant and automated processing
ai.body: About the use of AI in WattPrint:

items.automated: Wappi is an automated system. It is not a person, and nobody reads each answer before you see it.
items.estimates: Per-appliance figures are estimates. They are worked out from the main meter by an appliance-recognition model, not from separate meters, and are labelled “estimated”.
items.providers: Your question goes to the model providers (section 3) so Wappi can answer. We do not control what they do with it afterwards; weigh that before you ask.
items.training: Our appliance-recognition models are trained on public datasets (REFIT, Plegma, ENERTALK), not on your data.
